newsitem.title: USA: Revco to close 24 former Big B stores.
newsitem.headline: Revco to close 24 former Big B stores.

text.p: Revco D.S. Inc., which is in talks to be acquired by CVS Corp. said Wednesday it will close 24 drug stores in Georgia that it had acquired from Big B Inc. because they failed to meet profit guidelines.
Revco, the second-largest U.S. drugstore chain, paid $380 million in cash for Big B, which had 397 stores in the Southeast, in October.
Revco, based in Twinsburg, Ohio, said it will operate 141 stores in Georgia after the closings.
Workers affected by the closings will be offered jobs in neighbouring Revco stores wherever possible, the company said.
On Monday, Revco said it was in talks to be acquired by CVS, the nation's fifth-largest drug store chain.

Revco operates about 2,600 stores in 17 Midwestern, Southeastern and Eastern states. It employs nearly 40,000 people in its stores, six distribution centres, regional offices and corporate offices in suburban Cleveland.
Revco's stock fell 62.5 cents to $36.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
